cancer_indication: Extended adjuvant therapy for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer following adjuvant trastuzumab; and (with capecitabine) for metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after ≥2 prior anti-HER2 regimens.
moa: Neratinib is an irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor that covalently binds and inhibits EGFR, ERBB2 (HER2), and ERBB4 (HER4), preventing receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways. In human breast-cancer models and clinical contexts, this blockade suppresses proliferative and survival signaling and promotes apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest. In ER+/HER2+ disease, neratinib is described as complementing endocrine therapy, with clinical activity reported for combinations such as neratinib with fulvestrant and trastuzumab in ER+ metastatic disease with ERBB2 mutations.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.description: HER2/ERBB2 receptor tyrosine-kinase signaling that drives downstream proliferative and survival cascades.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.interpretation:
ERBB2 pathway activity is a core oncogenic dependency in HER2-driven breast cancer and is a key axis targeted by neratinib.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- HER2-amplified / HER2-mutant tumors have upregulated ERBB2 signalling and are “HER2-addicted”. Neratinib is an irreversible pan-HER TKI (HER1/2/4); high baseline HER2 signalling is required for benefit and predicts sensitivity, provided there is no dominant downstream bypass (e.g. TORC1, PI3K). (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: HER2-amplified/“ERBB2-addicted” breast cancer depends on ERBB2 kinase signaling; high baseline ERBB2 pathway activity predicts vulnerability to irreversible pan-HER inhibition by neratinib.
PMID:26874901; PMID:32678716; FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051); Reactome:R-HSA-1227986; MSigDB:M553 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Some ERBB2-high tumors are already “decoupled” downstream (e.g., PI3K pathway activation/PTEN loss), so ERBB2 inhibition incompletely shuts down survival signaling → relative resistance despite high ERBB2 signature.
PMID:20813970; PMID:26874901; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986; MSigDB:M553 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low bulk ERBB2 signature can still hide an actionable ERBB2 dependence (e.g., focal HER2-driven subclones or activating HER-family signaling states), where irreversible pan-HER blockade can still produce benefit.
PMID:26089701; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low ERBB2 pathway activity (non–HER2-driven breast cancer) implies minimal oncogenic reliance on ERBB2, so neratinib has little effective target.
FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051) (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Neratinib irreversibly inhibits HER-family kinase activity and reduces ERBB2 autophosphorylation → sustained shutdown of ERBB2 signal transduction in HER2-driven tumors → response.
PMID:27405796; FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051); Reactome:R-HSA-1227986 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even when ERBB2 signaling is inhibited, tumors can persist via bypass RTKs or downstream lesions (e.g., constitutive PI3K/mTOR output), yielding resistance despite ERBB2 “down” at the receptor layer.
PMID:20813970; PMID:33303839 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (functional): Neratinib cannot increase ERBB2 kinase signaling while occupying the ATP pocket covalently; an “up” ERBB2 signature would reflect expression/compensatory transcription, not increased signaling throughput.
PMID:27405796 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): Non-responders can show compensatory ERBB2/HER-family upregulation or rebound phosphorylation via network rewiring, but downstream escape keeps the phenotype resistant.
PMID:27405796; PMID:20813970 (PubMed)

REACTOME_MAPK1_MAPK3_SIGNALING.description: MAPK1/MAPK3 (ERK1/2) signaling downstream of activated receptor tyrosine kinases controlling proliferation and survival programs.
REACTOME_MAPK1_MAPK3_SIGNALING.interpretation:
MAPK/ERK output is a major downstream effector of EGFR/HER2 signaling in breast cancer and is part of the growth circuitry impacted by ERBB blockade.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- HER2 overexpression activates RAS→RAF→MEK→ERK. Neratinib suppresses HER2 and reduces pERK, producing growth arrest in HER2-dependent models. However, MAPK Up due to RAS/RAF mutations or alternative RTKs can maintain ERK signalling despite HER2 blockade and drive resistance. (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High ERK/MAPK output downstream of HER2 indicates growth-factor pathway addiction; blocking HER-family kinases can collapse MAPK signaling and inhibit proliferation in HER2-driven disease.
Reactome:R-HSA-5684996; MSigDB:M49146; PMID:27405796 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK pathway hyperactivation can be maintained by ERBB2-independent drivers (other RTKs or downstream lesions), so baseline MAPK “up” does not guarantee neratinib dependence.
Reactome:R-HSA-5684996; PMID:27405796 (Reactome)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A subset of HER2-driven tumors may have relatively lower ERK transcriptional output yet remain HER-family–dependent through parallel survival arms (e.g., PI3K), still allowing response to pan-HER blockade.
PMID:26089701; PMID:27405796 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low MAPK activity suggests limited reliance on the ERK cascade for proliferation, reducing the chance that upstream HER-family inhibition will be impactful.
Reactome:R-HSA-5684996 (Reactome)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective HER-family kinase blockade reduces downstream RAS–MEK–ERK signaling, contributing to tumor growth inhibition in HER2-dependent breast cancer.
PMID:27405796; Reactome:R-HSA-5684996 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK can remain suppressed yet tumors survive via alternate pathways (PI3K/mTOR, ER signaling in HR+ disease), producing resistance despite “down” ERK output.
PMID:20813970; PMID:18508484 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some responders can show transient compensatory ERK transcription signatures early, yet net pathway flux and tumor burden still fall (timing/biopsy effects).
Reactome:R-HSA-5684996 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Rebound MAPK activation via bypass RTKs or downstream lesions restores proliferative signaling despite HER-family inhibition → resistance.
Reactome:R-HSA-5684996; PMID:27405796 (Reactome)

REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING_IN_CANCER.description: PI3K–AKT signaling controlling cell survival and growth, frequently dysregulated in cancer via pathway alterations.
REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING_IN_CANCER.interpretation:
PI3K/AKT activity supports tumor survival and is highlighted as both a downstream node of HER signaling and a pathway that can shape response or escape to HER2-directed therapy in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Activating PIK3CA mutations or PTEN loss cause hyperactive PI3K/AKT signalling that can sustain growth even when HER2 is inhibited. In HER2+ breast cancer, PIK3CA mutations are repeatedly associated with lower pCR and reduced benefit from HER2-targeted regimens, and this is widely considered a resistance mechanism also relevant to neratinib. (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: When PI3K/AKT activity is HER2-driven (no strong downstream escape), upstream HER-family blockade can reduce PI3K signaling and produce response.
Reactome:R-HSA-2219528; MSigDB:M27162; PMID:27405796 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline PI3K pathway activation from PIK3CA mutation/PTEN loss can drive resistance to HER2-directed therapy because survival signaling persists downstream of receptor inhibition.
PMID:20813970; PMID:33303839 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2-addicted tumors have modest PI3K transcriptional signatures yet still depend on HER2 kinase activity for survival; receptor shutdown can still be effective.
PMID:27405796 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K/AKT pathway activity is common in tumors not reliant on HER-family signaling, reducing the likelihood of benefit from neratinib.
FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051) (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective HER-family blockade reduces upstream signaling into PI3K/AKT, contributing to tumor control in HER2-driven breast cancer.
PMID:27405796; Reactome:R-HSA-2219528 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K/AKT output can remain sufficient via parallel survival programs (mTORC1 or ER signaling), so tumors may resist despite partial PI3K downshift after neratinib.
PMID:18508484; PMID:33303839 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In responders, “up” can be a bulk signature artifact (e.g., immune/stromal admixture) while tumor cell PI3K flux is actually reduced.
Reactome:R-HSA-2219528 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive feedback (RTK rewiring) or constitutive lesions (PIK3CA/PTEN) sustain/increase AKT signaling despite HER-family inhibition → resistance.
PMID:20813970; PMID:33303839 (PubMed)

HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.description: mTORC1-driven anabolic growth and translation programs that integrate nutrient and growth-factor signals.
HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.interpretation:
mTORC1 signaling reflects tumor growth-state control downstream of AKT and is described as a relevant survival/growth axis in the neratinib mechanism and resistance context.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Sudhan et al. show that TORC1/mTORC1 hyperactivation drives neratinib resistance; PDX and cell-line models with high pS6/p4EBP1 are neratinib-resistant and can be resensitized by TORC1 inhibition (everolimus). By inference, tumors without marked mTORC1 hyperactivation (i.e. relatively lower TORC1 at baseline) remain more HER2-dependent and are more likely to be neratinib-sensitive. (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If mTORC1 elevation is largely upstream HER2/PI3K-driven (not autonomous), HER-family blockade can reduce inputs and improve control.
MSigDB:M5924; PMID:27405796 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High mTORC1 signaling can reflect downstream/parallel activation that blunts HER2-targeted efficacy (a rationale for adding mTOR/PI3K pathway inhibitors in resistant HER2+ disease).

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lower baseline mTORC1 can indicate fewer downstream escape mechanisms, increasing the chance that HER2 blockade alone is sufficient.
MSigDB:M5924 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors have low mTORC1 transcriptional output yet resist via MAPK/ER-driven proliferation or drug exposure limitations (pharmacology/tolerability).
MSigDB:M5924; FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051) (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: By suppressing upstream HER-family signaling, neratinib can reduce signaling into PI3K–AKT–mTOR networks and contribute to growth arrest in HER2-dependent tumors.
PMID:27405796; MSigDB:M5924 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even when mTORC1 signatures fall, tumors can survive via alternative programs (ER/MAPK) or incomplete pathway suppression, yielding resistance.
PMID:18508484; MSigDB:M5924 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Transient feedback activation of mTORC1 signatures can occur early while overall tumor burden decreases (sampling/timing effect).
MSigDB:M5924 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent mTORC1 activation after HER-family inhibition indicates downstream escape (PI3K/mTOR axis autonomy) and correlates with resistance.
PMID:20813970; PMID:33303839 (PubMed)

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-regulated transcriptional program linked to G1/S progression and proliferative cell-cycle activity.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation:
E2F-target activity captures proliferative drive and cell-cycle progression, which is discussed as changing with effective ERBB blockade and as a potential bypass route when sustained.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Neratinib clearly induces G1 arrest and reduces Cyclin D1/CDK4/6/E2F signalling in HER2-dependent models. Tumors that lack strong, autonomous cell-cycle deregulation (no RB loss, no massive CCND1/CDK4/6 hyperactivation) and rely mainly on HER2 for proliferation are more likely to be controlled by HER2 TKIs. A relatively lower baseline G2M/E2F score in a HER2-amplified tumor can be viewed as a favourable, but low-evidence feature. (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High E2F/cell-cycle transcription implies a proliferative, HER2-driven state that can be suppressed when upstream HER-family signaling is blocked.
MSigDB:M5925; PMID:33909203 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: E2F up can be maintained by RB pathway defects or alternative mitogenic drivers, so proliferation persists even when HER2 is inhibited → resistance.
MSigDB:M5925 (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2-driven tumors are less overtly proliferative at baseline (treatment effects/dormancy) but still HER-family dependent; pathway blockade can still be beneficial.
PMID:27405796 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low E2F targets suggests limited reliance on active cycling; HER2 inhibition may not translate into meaningful cytostatic effect.
MSigDB:M5925 (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Neratinib reduces HER-family signaling and cell-cycle regulatory programs, driving G1 arrest and lowering E2F target expression in sensitive HER2-driven models.
PMID:33909203; MSigDB:M5925 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: E2F may drop (cytostasis) without tumor regression if survival pathways persist (PI3K/mTOR/ER), yielding stable but resistant disease.
PMID:20813970; PMID:18508484 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In responders, bulk “up” E2F can reflect proliferating immune/stromal cells or sampling bias while tumor cell cycling is actually curtailed.
MSigDB:M5925 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to suppress E2F targets after neratinib implies ongoing proliferation (RB/E2F axis uncoupled from HER2), consistent with resistance.
MSigDB:M5925; PMID:33909203 (gsea-msigdb.org)

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Core apoptotic machinery and pro-death signaling programs that execute programmed cell death.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation:
Apoptosis is a key tumor-control outcome described with HER-family signaling inhibition, reflecting a shift away from survival signaling in responsive settings.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Neratinib induces apoptosis in HER2-dependent cancer cells (caspase activation, PARP cleavage). Tumors that are “apoptotically primed” (higher pro-apoptotic signalling / lower anti-apoptotic buffering) are more likely to undergo cell death once HER2 and its downstream survival signals are blocked, so a higher apoptosis gene-set at baseline is a plausible (though not yet validated) sensitivity feature. (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A primed apoptotic state (high pro-apoptotic signaling) can facilitate rapid tumor cell death once oncogenic HER-family survival signaling is removed.
MSigDB:M5902; PMID:27405796 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis signatures can be elevated from stress/inflammation but neutralized by strong anti-apoptotic programs, so baseline “up” does not ensure drug sensitivity.
MSigDB:M5902 (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low apoptosis at baseline is common in aggressive HER2-driven tumors; removing HER-family survival signaling can still trigger apoptosis in sensitive disease.
PMID:33909203; MSigDB:M5902 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong baseline apoptosis suppression (e.g., anti-apoptotic buffering) can limit cell death even if HER2 is inhibited, contributing to resistance.
MSigDB:M5902 (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Neratinib’s sustained HER-family inhibition can lead to cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in sensitive HER2-driven settings.
PMID:33909203; PMID:27405796; MSigDB:M5902 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis gene expression can rise (stress response) without effective execution (caspase blockade), resulting in resistant phenotype despite “up” signature.
MSigDB:M5902 (gsea-msigdb.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In deep responders with rapid tumor cell clearance, bulk tumor apoptosis signatures may fall over time as tumor mass contracts.
MSigDB:M5902 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce apoptosis after HER-family blockade implies continued survival signaling (PI3K/mTOR or ER escape), consistent with resistance.
PMID:20813970; PMID:18508484 (PubMed)

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.description: Estrogen receptor (ER)-linked transcriptional program reflecting sustained/late ER-driven gene expression.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.interpretation:
ER signaling is described as clinically relevant in HR+ breast cancer subtypes where cross-talk with HER2 can influence benefit and where combination endocrine strategies are discussed alongside neratinib.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In HR+/HER2+ or HER2-low BC, strong ER signalling can sustain proliferation when HER2 is inhibited, contributing to suboptimal response to HER2-directed therapy alone. Preclinical and emerging clinical data support triple combinations (neratinib + endocrine therapy + CDK4/6i) to overcome this. Thus, baseline estrogen-response Up is unfavourable for neratinib alone, but compatible with sensitivity when combined with appropriate endocrine ± CDK4/6 blockade. (Nature)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (HR+/HER2+ context): In ER+/HER2+ early breast cancer, HR positivity is a key clinical stratum where extended adjuvant neratinib shows benefit; ER/HER2 co-dependence can make sustained HER blockade valuable.
PMID:26874901; PMID:33183970; MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong ER program can act as an escape axis in HR+/HER2+ disease via ER–HER2 crosstalk, potentially reducing reliance on HER2 signaling alone and promoting relative resistance unless ER is also controlled.
PMID:18508484; PMID:274338?? (not used); MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: HR-low/weak ER signaling in a HER2-driven tumor can increase dependence on HER-family pathways, making HER blockade more effective.
MSigDB:M5907; PMID:27405796 (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If ER signaling is low and HER2 signaling is not dominant (non–HER2-driven biology), neratinib is unlikely to help.
FDA label (NERLYNX/neratinib; NDA 208051) (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In some responding HR+/HER2+ tumors, ER transcriptional programs can transiently rise as feedback while HER2 signaling is effectively suppressed and disease still improves (timing effect).
PMID:18508484; MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive ER upregulation after HER2 blockade is a known escape mechanism in HR+/HER2+ breast cancer, supporting resistance unless combined ER-directed therapy is optimized.
PMID:18508484; PMID:20887199; MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: If HER2 blockade is paired with effective endocrine control (or ER program contracts), reduced ER-driven escape alongside HER-family inhibition supports sensitivity in HR+/HER2+ disease.
PMID:18508484; PMID:33183970; MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ER signatures can fall (e.g., due to tumor dedifferentiation or sampling) while non-ER escape pathways (PI3K/mTOR/MAPK) still maintain resistance.
PMID:20813970; MSigDB:M5907 (PubMed)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Higher HER2 dependence (amplification/overexpression or activating ERBB2 context as described) is presented as a setting where neratinib’s direct ERBB2 inhibition is most effective.
PIK3CA alterations are explicitly described as being associated with enhanced benefit from neratinib in ExteNET (noted as counterintuitive in the source).

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Upregulated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling driven by PIK3CA mutation is described as a bypass survival mechanism that can reduce neratinib efficacy when the pathway remains high.
Upregulation of alternate tyrosine-kinase signaling via ERBB3 is described as a mechanism to reactivate AKT/MAPK and bypass HER2 blockade.
Upregulation of IGF1R signaling is described as an alternative receptor input that can restore downstream survival signaling despite ERBB inhibition.
Upregulation of HGF–MET signaling is described as a bypass route to reactivate AKT/MAPK and support resistance to HER2 inhibition.
Elevated Cyclin D1/E2F axis activity (including CCND1 amplification as stated) is described as enabling proliferation and overcoming neratinib-induced growth suppression.
Upregulation of Cyclin D1–CDK4 signaling is described as sustaining RB phosphorylation/E2F activation and promoting resistance to neratinib’s antiproliferative effects.
Overexpression of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family signaling is described as a survival mechanism that can blunt neratinib-induced cell death.
TNF-linked inflammatory survival signaling (via TNFα/NFκB framing in the source) is described as a potential escape program under chronic neratinib exposure.
Upregulation of IL6-associated survival signaling (with STAT3 noted) is described as a potential resistance mechanism supporting survival under HER2 inhibition.
STAT3-associated survival signaling is described as part of an inflammatory/pro-survival program that may help cells resist neratinib-induced death.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: PTEN loss is described as hyperactivating PI3K/AKT and mTORC1 signaling, enabling bypass survival signaling and contributing to resistance.
RB1 loss is described as allowing bypass of neratinib’s antiproliferative effects by sustaining E2F-driven proliferation.
Loss or downregulation of p53 function (including TP53 mutation context) is described as limiting apoptotic responses to ERBB2 inhibition and contributing to resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer: Neratinib is approved as extended adjuvant therapy for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer (following trastuzumab); US indication covers early-stage HER2-overexpressing disease after adjuvant trastuzumab, while EU approval limits it to hormone receptor–positive HER2+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer: In 2020, the FDA approved neratinib (with capecitabine) for metastatic HER2+ breast cancer after ≥2 prior anti-HER2 regimens.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer w: As of 2023, NCCN advises neratinib use (often with fulvestrant and trastuzumab) in HER2-negative metastatic patients with activating ERBB2 mutations.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.ER+/HER2+ disease: Neratinib may complement endocrine therapy in hormone-receptor–positive subtypes, with greater benefit described in HR+ patients and with combination endocrine blockade (e.g., neratinib, fulvestrant, trastuzumab) reported to yield objective responses in ER+ metastatic disease with ERBB2 mutation context.
